newsitem.title: NEPAL: Relatives of Nepali victims to fly to India.
newsitem.headline: Relatives of Nepali victims to fly to India.

text.p: Relatives of the Nepali victims of the world's worst mid-air collision will fly to New Delhi to identify the bodies, Saudi airline officials said on Thursday.
Officials said 53 Nepalis were among the 349 victims of the crash between a Saudia Airlines Boeing 747 and a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 freighter near Delhi on Tuesday.
On Wednesday the foreign ministry had put the figure at 45 amid conflicting information.

"Full assistance will be provided by the Saudi airlines to either arrange cremation in India or bring the bodies to Nepal as per the relatives wishes," said Achyut Shrestha of Air Express Private Ltd, general sales agent for Saudia in Nepal.
Shrestha told Reuters the Saudi airline would pay for one family member of each victim to travel to India for the identification of the bodies.
"We have contacted the families and asked them to get in touch with us so we can make arrangements for their travel," he said.
Many Nepali workers, mainly manual labourers, plumbers and drivers, travel to Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries in search of employment.
Government officials said there were about 8,500 Nepali workers in Saudi Arabia, but analysts said the number could be twice as high because many people went there without informing the government.

Nepal is one of the 10 poorest countries in the world and remittances from workers abroad are a major source of foreign exchange earnings in a country that receives 60 percent of its development budget in foreign aid.
Officials said they did not have records of the amount of money sent home by workers from the Middle East as they did not keep separate records of such transactions.
